question: Your team uses Claude Code in a repository with three files in .claude/rules/. Their YAML frontmatter fields set paths: ["terraform/**/*"], paths: ["**/*.test.tsx"], and paths: ["db/migrations/**/*.sql"]. In a new session, an engineer asks Claude Code to edit only the file src/components/Button.tsx. Which statement correctly describes how these rule files load into context during this edit?

options.text: All three rule files load at session start, because Claude Code reads every file in .claude/rules/ into context for each session.
options.reason: The paths field makes a rule conditional. A path-scoped rule loads only when a matching file is edited, not at the start of every session.

options.text: Only the testing rule loads, because Button.tsx has the .tsx extension that appears in the **/*.test.tsx glob pattern.
options.reason: The pattern **/*.test.tsx matches only files whose names end in .test.tsx. Button.tsx does not match, so the testing rule stays out of context.

options.text: None of the three rule files loads, because Button.tsx matches none of their paths glob patterns.
options.reason: Path-scoped rules load only when Claude Code edits files that match their glob patterns. Button.tsx matches none of the three patterns, so none of these rules adds context or token usage.

options.text: All three rule files load, and Claude Code then decides by itself which conventions are relevant to the edited component file.
options.reason: Path scoping keeps non-matching rules out of context, which reduces irrelevant context and token usage. Claude Code does not load every rule and then filter the rules afterward.
